ledger: 00:00–00:03: Foreground phone display is out of focus; apparent large digits are not used for character-level comparison.
00:03.25–00:06.25: Phone's central readout resembles an angular, malformed A-like glyph followed by '7.42'; moving glare intermittently obscures characters.
00:06.75, 00:07.25–00:07.75, 00:08.25–00:08.75: Sharp central phone readout consistently shows the same malformed A-like prefix and '7.42'; no supported character change.
00:06.75 and 00:08.25: Below the main readout, the phone label reads approximately 'AZ-12', with an additional tiny overlapping glyph above it; unchanged between these clear views.
00:04.25 and 00:06.75: Upper phone heading consists of two A-like characters with a detached horizontal stroke between/above them; no coherent word is readable.
00:06.75: Top-left phone status text resembles '7A2'; top-center text resembles '4.4' followed by a malformed mark. These are approximate transcriptions of irregular glyphs.
00:09.00–00:09.75: Phone tilts away and exits; darkening, blur, and cropping prevent further reliable text comparison.

findings.description: At 00:06.75, the sharply visible phone interface contains a malformed A-like character prefixed to the large '7.42' readout, an upper heading made of A-like glyphs and a floating stroke, and a lower 'AZ-12'-like label with an overlapping miniature glyph above it. Together these form garbled interface text rather than coherent clock/status labels. The same malformed forms remain clearly visible at 00:08.25, so the defect is not caused by passing glare or motion blur. No unexplained change between legible readings is established.
